group_scores.rationale: No systemic trade or fiscal shock in the window. The US-China truce roll-over to about 2027-01-10 predates the window and is background. No in-window tariff proclamation was found in FR or White House listings, and no foreign-holder tax revival in Treasury, Ways and Means or Senate Finance listings. Appropriations are moving toward the Dec 11 CR expiry. Evidence is primary-source and largely by absence; no T2 press checked.
group_scores.falsifier: A T2-confirmed new broad US tariff action or Section 122 replacement in the window, a Section 899-style withholding revival, or a US-China truce breakdown before the January cliff.

group_scores.rationale: No new tariff proclamation, CIT IEEPA refund ruling or China escalation in the window. All twelve Senate FY27 bills are public (verified) and Chair Cole aims to avoid a shutdown (verified), but the Dec 11 deadline is outside the window and no T2 coverage was found. CAPE refunds continue as background.
group_scores.falsifier: A T2-reported impasse making a post-Dec 11 lapse likely, a Section 899-style provision in a lame-duck vehicle, or a new Section 232 rate reported by T2 press for 14-20 Nov.

group_scores.rationale: Truce elements (China's 24% suspension, US Section 301 port fees, BIS affiliates rule) were rolled to about 2027-01-10 before the window: background. In the window MOFCOM was conciliatory and no US escalatory action was found. The BIS remote-access rule (verified on the FR API, effective 2026-11-19) is an adverse severity-2 item for D:5-headquartered AI/cloud firms, but it is single-issuer and its market impact is unconfirmed by T2, so it does not support a nonzero score.
group_scores.falsifier: No US instrument on the China reciprocal baseline (moot after the IEEPA ruling) turning into a new tariff, new entity listings, rare-earth licensing slippage, a final MOFCOM EU dairy duty, or T2 reports that the remote-access rule materially hits Chinese AI and cloud names.

group_scores.rationale: DG Trade shows no change to the EU-US framework, no 232 move on EU goods, no retaliation and no EU-China escalation for 14-20 Nov. The only in-window item is routine AD duties on cold-rolled steel from Asia and Turkiye (verified). Trade news does not explain VGK -2.06%; no US-side T2 check was possible.
group_scores.falsifier: A US tariff action on EU goods or EU countermeasure dated 14-20 Nov confirmed by USTR, FR or T2 press; a final MOFCOM dairy duty; or a costly EU ferroalloy safeguard.

group_scores.rationale: In-window FR items are routine AD/CVD orders (freight rail couplers, hardwood plywood). Section 232 Proclamation 11077 on robotics and machinery predates the window and sets no rate. EU cold-rolled steel duties are a marginal input-cost item.
group_scores.falsifier: A Section 232 rate on machinery, trucks or metals announced in the window, or a 232 change on EU autos or steel.

group_scores.rationale: No in-window trade development explains EEM +3.75% (z 1.95). The new BIS license requirement for advanced chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil (verified) is a mild ASEAN headwind, with US-headquartered firms exempt; single issuer, no T2. The Thailand deal is unsigned. Truce roll-over is background.
group_scores.falsifier: T2 reports that the BIS license regime stalls ASEAN data-center capex, a renewed US-China tariff threat, or evidence of a persistent trade or policy driver behind the EM rally.
